articles.title: Man jailed for piloting small boat carrying 26 others to Kent coast
articles.summary: Jemal Abdela was sentenced after pleading guilty to endangering 26 others, including six children.
articles.body:
A man has been jailed for 18 months for piloting a small boat carrying 26 other people, including six children, towards the Kent coast.

Jemal Abdela, 32, was sentenced after pleading guilty to the offence of endangering others during a sea crossing to the UK without valid entry clearance on July 25.

Winchester Crown Court heard Abdela, who is Eritrean, had also attempted to disguise the fact he had been driving the black inflatable across the Channel when it was approached by immigration officers.

A Home Office spokesman said Abdela was the 20th small boat pilot to be imprisoned in four months for endangering lives at sea .

Matthew Parris, prosecuting, told the court that the defendant was seen piloting the boat, which was being followed by French authorities.

He said Abdela had "dived into the centre of the boat and moved to another location wearing a hat" before being identified, adding that the vessel did not have flares, GPS or maps onboard.

The court heard that Abdela told police he had paid €800 (£680) for the crossing, which had begun at 17:00 BST the previous day.

He also claimed to have been sat by the captain of the boat, but was then made to take over control of the vessel by the other passengers.

Francesca Hallett, defending, said that Abdela had managed to "escape" war-torn Eritrea, where he was born.

She said that he first went to the Ethiopian capital, Addis Ababa, but was imprisoned because of his Eritrean nationality.

He then went on to travel through Sudan and Egypt to Libya where he was captured and tortured by people smugglers for eight months and was later freed.

Hallett added that Abdela moved on to Italy and France, both of which he described as "not safe for refugees".

"At that stage he felt the UK was the safest option," she said.

Sentencing Abdela, Judge James Bromige said that he would "ordinarily" be deported on completion of his time in prison.

Anna Turley, Minister for Border Security and Asylum, called Abdela a "reckless criminal" who had been "rightly jailed".

articles.title: Iraq grants Iranian airlines 40 daily Najaf flights after US exemption
articles.summary: Mahan Air is excluded from the agreement as Baghdad says Washington granted its request for a waiver.
articles.body:
Iraq has agreed to let Iranian airlines, except Mahan Air, operate up to 40 flights a day to and from Najaf International Airport, saying the United States granted an exemption from its sanctions.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s office announced the agreement on Friday, a day after Tehran urged Baghdad to lift restrictions that it said hurt pilgrims, patients, students and business.

The deal eases the links between the two Shia-majority neighbours since Washington sanctioned Iran’s aviation sector last month.

Al-Zaidi welcomed the “positive response shown by the US government to Iraq’s efforts and its cooperation in granting the necessary exemption”, the statement from his office said.

“Air travel does not merely represent transportation between two airports, but rather a bridge of communication between peoples,” it added.

Separately, Iraq’s Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the return of flights supports an Iraqi-US partnership premised on mutual respect.

Hussein also welcomed what he described as US understanding of the importance of respecting religious freedom and facilitating access for visitors to holy sites.

The US Treasury announced sanctions on September 8 against 36 entities linked to Iran’s aviation sector .

Foreign ground-handling companies then refused to service Iranian aircraft for fear of falling foul of US sanctions, and flights stopped at four Iraqi airports.

Soon after, Iraq’s government held direct talks with Washington, seeking an exemption.

Iraq’s ambassador to Tehran, Yasser al-Hajjaj, told Iran’s IRNA news agency that Baghdad had not ordered the halt in flights. The suspension also led to demonstrations outside Najaf airport and in Nasiriya, Karbala and Amarah, according to Iran’s Press TV.

Najaf is the main destination for Iranian flights in Iraq. Flights to and from the city carry Iraqi Shia Muslim pilgrims to Iran’s holy cities or Iranians visiting sacred sites in Iraq.

Iran’s ambassador to Baghdad, Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh, told the Iranian news agency ISNA that there were “roughly 25 daily flights from Iran to Najaf and about 15 flights to Baghdad” before the ban.

“Around 12,000 to 13,000 people travel between Iran and Iraq and vice versa on Iranian airlines, which is not a small number,” he added.

In a statement shared on Thursday, Iran’s Foreign Ministry said that Washington’s “illegal and inhumane” extraterritorial enforcement of sanctions was disrupting Iran’s trade and air transport.

Flights between Najaf and Iran restarted late on Monday, according to the Iraqi News Agency.

However, flights with Iran are still suspended at Baghdad, Erbil and Sulaimaniyah airports, forcing passengers into land journeys of at least 12 hours and disrupting pilgrim traffic.

Al Jazeera has not verified the exemption with representatives in Washington.

articles.title: Cases clubbed only after CJI spoke to presiding judges
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The sound and fury in the Supreme Court Wednesday over the clubbing of two petitions - one seeking the initiation of contempt proceedings for
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The sound and fury in the Supreme Court Wednesday over the clubbing of two petitions - one seeking the initiation of contempt proceedings for the violation of an earlier SC judgement and the other challenging the validity of a new law - both on the deputation of IPS officers in the central armed police forces (CAPFs), has turned out to be much ado about nothing.The contempt petition was initiated for the alleged violation of the SC's May 23, 2025, judgement directing the gradual reduction and eventual phasing out of IPS officers' deputation to CAPFs and is pending before a bench headed by Justice Ujjal Bhuyan.Another petition, which challenged the validity of the new CAPF Act, which was enacted subsequent to the SC judgement and permitted the deputation of IPS officers to CAPFs, is before another bench headed by Justice Manoj Misra.On September 30, the contempt petition listed before Justice Bhuyan was abruptly dropped from the notified list of cases, and, subsequently, both the contempt petition and the writ petition were listed before a special bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan. This led to an uproar before the special bench. Senior advocate Shyam Divan said, "You cannot have a listed matter plucked off the board. This is an all-India court. People make travel arrangements and come here from all over the country. Why should a matter which is listed be removed during the course of the day? Once the cause list is mentioned and notified in the Supreme Court of India, no one can fiddle with it." Senior advocate Guru Krishna Kumar echoed Divan's grievance.However, it transpired that additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati had requested that the two petitions be clubbed and be placed for hearing before any one of the two benches on the ground that the new law was the defence of the Union govt in contempt and suggested that it would be better if the two cases were heard together.SC registry sources said following this, the CJI consulted the presiding judges - Justices Misra and Bhuyan - before constituting the special bench and placing both the matters before it.However, Justice Misra faulted the ASG for not informing the opposite side prior to making the request to the CJI, which led to such a situation. The CJI could not be contacted, as he is abroad.The SC registry, from which an explanation was sought, filed a report on clubbing of the two cases. The bench of Justices Misra and Bhuyan said in its order, "The explanation tendered by the registry is accepted and taken on record. The same shall be kept in a sealed cover by the concerned section." It posted both the contempt petition and the writ petition for hearing together on Oct 15.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Latin America sees China as more positive global influence than US: Poll
articles.summary: Annual Latinobarometro survey finds views of China’s influence improving as perceptions of US influence worsen.
articles.body:
China is perceived more positively as a global influence than the United States in Latin America, according to a new regional survey, in a first since the poll began in 1995.

The 2026 Latinobarometro survey published on Friday found that 65 percent of respondents in 17 countries saw China as a positive influence. That was compared with 57 percent who said the same of the US.

Support for China has risen sharply since 2020, when 48 percent of respondents viewed its influence positively. The figure for the US has fallen from 60 percent over the same period.

Costa Rica and the Dominican Republic were the only countries surveyed where respondents viewed US influence more positively than China’s.

Latinobarometro, a Chile-based nonprofit organisation, conducts annual surveys across the region on issues including democracy, the economy, security and migration.

The findings come during US President Donald Trump’s second term, as his administration has sought to strengthen Washington’s influence in Latin America, particularly through exercising more military might.

That has included conducting strikes on alleged drug smuggling boats in the region, which rights groups have decried as extrajudicial killings, and abducting Venezuela’s then-leader Nicolas Maduro in Brazil.

Trump has described his approach as the “ Donroe Doctrine ”.

Despite the findings on global influence, the US remained more popular than China when respondents were asked about their overall views of the two countries.

Some 63 percent of respondents said they had a favourable opinion of the US, compared with 58 percent for China. The US figure was down from 73 percent in 2024.

The survey also asked respondents about the US military capture of Maduro .

A majority in all but one country, Argentina, approved of Maduro’s capture by US forces.

Views were more divided over what the operation meant for Venezuela, with 35 percent saying removing Maduro had benefitted the country and 28 percent saying it had harmed it.

Venezuelans were among the populations most likely to view US influence positively, according to the survey.

The 2026 survey was based on about 19,200 face-to-face interviews conducted in 17 countries between May 7 and June 17, with a margin of error of 1 percent.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: At a time when vigilante groups are active in stopping cattle smuggling purportedly to prevent slaughter, the Supreme Court has ruled that the police cannot presumptively invoke stringent provisions of anti-cattle slaughter laws against people for mere illegal transportation of bovine animals.Acquitting a person convicted by a trial court and Chhattisgarh HC for illegally transporting 32 bulls under Chhattisgarh Agricultural Cattle Preservation Act, 2004, a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said police have failed to establish the intention of the accused that cattle were being transported for slaughter. articles.title: Christa Pike unconscious, on ventilator after botched execution: Lawyers
articles.summary: The Tennessee woman’s legal team says doctors are working to clear doses of the drug pentobarbital from her system.
articles.body:
Christa Pike has been placed on a ventilator and intubated after surviving a failed execution attempt, according to a court filing from her lawyers.

The Tennessee woman, they wrote on Friday, “remains critically ill” and is unconscious while receiving treatment at a hospital in Nashville.

According to the filing, medical staff are working to save Pike’s life and clear her system of the two doses of the drug pentobarbital, which the US state uses to execute prisoners.

“Upon arrival, both of her arms were swollen, burned, and blistered,” Pike’s lawyers wrote about the drug’s effects on her body.

The filing, which was part of an emergency request by Pike’s lawyers to preserve state records related to her execution, marks the most detailed update on Pike’s condition after she was transported by ambulance to hospital from a Tennessee prison on Wednesday, following the botched attempt.

Pike’s lawyers argued that problems with the IV lines caused the pentobarbital to flow into her body instead of her bloodstream.

“Apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed or that the veins had blown and that the pentobarbital was, in whole or in part, entering Ms Pike’s body,” they wrote.

The lawyers allege prison staff prepared “a backup set of syringes” and “administered another lethal dose of pentobarbital”.

Pike, who was sentenced to death at 18 after she was found guilty of torturing and murdering another young woman in 1995, would have been the first woman in more than 200 years to be executed in Tennessee. She was also the only woman on the state’s death row.

Pike’s lawyers have called for her sentence to be commuted to life in prison after she endured what they called “chemical torture”.

Tennessee’s Governor Bill Lee has suspended all executions for the rest of the year while the state investigates what happened.

articles.title: UK man accused of planning terrorism acts against Nigel Farage also charged in murder of another politician
articles.summary: British prosecutors charged Ann Widdecombe murder suspect Joshua Kerry with preparing terrorist acts allegedly targeting Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.
articles.body: British prosecutors announced terrorism charges Friday against a 28-year-old man already in custody for the alleged murder of a conservative politician. The Crown Prosecution Service charged Joshua Kerry of South Yorkshire with one count of preparation of terrorist acts, accusing him of "engaging in conduct in preparation of acts of terrorism, including against [Reform UK leader] Nigel Farage MP." Kerry has been in the custody of His Majesty's government since late July, after he was arrested and accused of murdering former Reform UK and Conservative politician Ann Widdecombe. Prosecutors say Widdecombe was eating lunch in her Devon home July 8, when Kerry allegedly walked through the front door, beat her 21 times in the head with a hammer, took her wallet and was gone in an attack that lasted only two minutes. IRAN PROBED IN ALLEGED TERRORISM PLOT AT UK BASE Authorities say the latest charges against Kerry are related to events between May 31 and July 8. In a statement, Senior National Coordinator for Counterterrorism Policing, Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, said, "The charge announced today is a result of the tireless work of investigators across the Counterterrorism Policing network. This investigation has been led by a dedicated team of detectives, analysts and forensic experts, working on multiple lines of inquiry, which has resulted in this very serious charge." U.K. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, posting on X, called the new charges against Kerry "extremely concerning" and sent her "profound sympathies" to the Farage family. She added that "an attack on anyone in politics is an attack on us all. This case raises serious questions about the security of those in public life." The Jo Cox Foundation, set up in honor of the Labour MP who was murdered in 2016, said in a statement, "No one in public life should have to fear for their safety. Violence, abuse and intimidation not only endangered individuals and their families, but threaten our democracy and have no place in public life. We must do more to prevent the rising levels of abuse and intimidation in politics." Kerry is due back at Westminster Magistrates’ Court Wednesday. Separately on Friday, Counterterrorism Policing announced charges against two Iranian men accused of plotting "to target the Jewish community in the Manchester area." The Crown Prosecution Service charged 36-year-old Salam Ahmadyan and 34-year-old Rahman Salehi with "engaging in conduct in preparation for terrorist acts, contrary to Section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006," alleging that two men were "in contact with an overseas third-party who may be in Iran in relation to the plot." SUSPECT CHARGED IN MURDER OF UK POLITICIAN ANNE WIDDECOMBE Evans called the charges "extremely serious" while reiterating that "we do not believe there to be any ongoing threat to the public in relation to this matter." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Evans noted the alleged plot comes during the High Holy Day period and "coincides with the anniversary of the devastating terrorist attack last year at Heaton Park synagogue and comes in a wider context of increasing antisemitic incidents across the U.K." Ahmadyan and Salehi have been remanded and are scheduled to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court Saturday. articles.title: FlyDubai co-pilot accused of cockpit attack was grounded by Oman Air before joining airline: report
articles.summary: The FlyDubai co-pilot was reportedly grounded by Oman Air in 2024 over visits to radical Islamic websites before being hired without a background check.
articles.body: The FlyDubai co-pilot accused of stabbing the captain of a passenger jet mid-flight and nearly causing a catastrophic crash was grounded by Oman Air in 2024 after the airline discovered he had been visiting radical Islamic websites, according to a source familiar with the matter. Authorities believe the co-pilot moved to Dubai later that same year, according to the source, who also told Fox News the co-pilot spent a significant part of his life outside Oman, including with his mother, who is from Syria. According to the source, FlyDubai did not check with Oman Air about the co-pilot before hiring him. FLYDUBAI PILOT SHOWED WORLD 'THE HIGHEST FORM OF COURAGE,' INDIA'S PM SAYS The new details come as The Wall Street Journal reported Friday, citing people familiar with the matter, that the Omani national had previously been banned from flying over concerns he had adopted radical ideological views before later being hired by FlyDubai. The newspaper reported it was unclear whether Omani officials shared those concerns with other countries or airlines. Fox News has not independently verified the reason the co-pilot was grounded by Oman Air. The alleged attack unfolded Wednesday aboard FlyDubai Flight 1073 as the aircraft traveled from Dubai to Tel Aviv. UNITED FLIGHT FROM CHICAGO MAKES EMERGENCY LANDING AFTER PASSENGER'S 'MULTIPLE ATTEMPTS' TO BREACH COCKPIT According to passengers and officials, the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain inside the cockpit, sending the aircraft into a steep dive that nearly tore it apart before two reserve pilots aboard the flight regained control and safely diverted the aircraft to Saudi Arabia. Passengers and crew members then helped overpower the suspect, according to accounts of the incident. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday described the incident as terrorism, saying the attacker had undergone "Islamic radicalization." "He came to crash the passengers on board," Netanyahu said, according to the Wall Street Journal. UK AIRBASE TERROR SUSPECTS BEING RELEASED ON BAIL AS IRAN DENIES CONNECTION Netanyahu also said Israeli authorities are investigating whether the suspect acted alone or had assistance from others. The United Arab Emirates is leading the investigation into the incident. A UAE spokesperson declined to comment to the Journal on the suspect's background, saying officials did not want to prejudice the outcome of the investigation or interfere with its course. The incident has prompted renewed scrutiny of airline pilot vetting procedures and aviation security on flights serving Israel. Aviation security analysts told the Journal the episode represented a significant security failure and raised questions about how warning signs may have gone undetected before the co-pilot entered the cockpit. FlyDubai has suspended flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv following the attack. articles.body: NEW DELHI: In what is intended to remove any ambiguity or misplaced perception regarding certain land areas, peaks, mountains, passes, glaciers and water bodies in Ladakh, including those bordering China, being an integral part of India, the government has, in consultation with the UT, identified 28 places and features in Ladakh by standard names on the official map of the Survey of India.Among the 28 are places in Aksai Chin and Gilgit-Baltistan in POK, which India treats as part of Ladakh."Identifying them formally... is aimed at facilitating their accurate recognition and better awareness among the people at large," the home ministry said Friday.The move comes less than a couple of months after a similar step was taken with regard to 27 border areas and passes in Arunachal Pradesh.Among the 28 places in Ladakh identified are 10 peaks, three mountains, seven land areas, two glaciers, two passes, one river, one lake, one water body and one valley. articles.title: Federal court temporarily blocks Trump administration’s border wall in Texas’ Big Bend region
articles.summary: A federal court in Texas on Friday issued a ruling temporarily blocking the Trump administration from building a border wall and other infrastructure across the state’s Big Bend region.
articles.body: WASHINGTON — A federal court in Texas on Friday issued a ruling temporarily blocking the Trump administration from building a border wall and other infrastructure across the state’s Big Bend region. The news marks a major win for landowners, businesses and environmentalists in the region who have united to oppose the planned infrastructure projects, which are part of a $46 billion effort by the Trump administration to line the southern border with a mix of 30-foot-tall steel walls, vehicle barriers, roads and surveillance technology. Judge Kathleen Cardone said in her ruling that the plaintiffs were “likely to succeed on the merits of at least one of the claims in suit, that there is a likelihood that they will suffer serious, irreparable harm without an injunction, and that the balance of the equities and the public interest weigh in their favor.” Customs and Border Protection and the Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Opponents of the border wall project have argued that the Big Bend region of Texas is so remote and the landscape so rugged that it serves as its own deterrent to illegal immigration and that the administration violated the law when it issued a swath of waivers allowing it to bypass numerous regulations in order to speed up border wall infrastructure projects. Laiken Jordahl, with the Center of Biological Diversity that brought the suit, called Cardone’s ruling a “total victory.” “The bulldozers are going to be sent packing until she rules on the merits,” Jordahl said. “This is such a historic day for Big Bend and for Texas and the Constitution.” The court’s decision comes just weeks after the administration erected the first border wall panels in the Big Bend sector in the middle of September. The border wall project through the Big Bend sector has sparked bipartisan opposition. Much of the opposition has been geared around Customs and Border Protection’s plans for inside the Big Bend National Park, which is prized for its beautiful landscapes, limestone cliffs and crystal clear night sky views. When bulldozers were spotted clearing land in the park in August, it sparked widespread opposition with both Republicans and Democrats calling for the administration to stop. Customs and Border Protection paused all activity there, but that pause expired on September 30. The administration has said it’s reevaluating plans for the National Park but has so far not said what it will do there. But the judge’s ruling also extends to areas up and downriver from the National Park, where Customs and Border Protection has planned a range of border infrastructure projects that would largely require build across privately owned land.

articles.title: Death row inmate unconscious on ventilator after botched execution for teen’s killing: attorneys
articles.summary: Christa Pike remains unconscious on a ventilator after Tennessee's botched lethal injection as attorneys file to preserve execution evidence.
articles.body: A Tennessee death row inmate remained unconscious on a ventilator Friday after surviving the state's failed attempt to execute her this week, and her attorneys accused prison officials of ignoring months of warnings that the lethal injection could go catastrophically wrong. Christa Pike was scheduled to be executed for the 1995 torture killing of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. She would have become the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years before Wednesday night's execution attempt failed. Pike's attorneys filed an emergency motion in Davidson County Chancery Court seeking an order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve evidence related to what they described as the state's "botched attempted execution." "She is critically ill, unconscious, intubated and receiving breathing assistance through a ventilator," they added. "She is being treated for the serious effects of the pentobarbital administered during the execution attempt, including significant injuries to both arms." MULTIPLE DEATH SENTENCES IN DIFFERENT STATES ARE SET TO BE CARRIED OUT WITHIN 24 HOURS: 'NOT VERY COMMON' The emergency motion paints a far more detailed picture of what Pike's attorneys say unfolded inside the execution chamber. "Her concerns were called 'speculation'; they were laughed off, scoffed at, and dismissed," the motion states. articles.title: The Flydubai attack suspect was removed by another airline over concerns about his extremist views, sources say
articles.summary: The pilot suspected of having attacked another pilot aboard a Tel Aviv-bound Flydubai flight on Wednesday was removed from a previous job at Oman’s national airline last year following concerns about his extremist views, sources familiar with the matter told CNN.
articles.body: The pilot suspected of having attacked another pilot aboard a Tel Aviv-bound Flydubai flight on Wednesday was removed from a previous job at Oman’s national airline last year following concerns about his extremist views, sources familiar with the matter told CNN. A regional diplomatic source familiar with the matter told CNN the suspect was removed from training because of concerns he had radical views. The source said he was given another role at the airline, Oman Air. The pilot is an Omani citizen, another source said. He was born in the United Arab Emirates to an Omani father and Syrian mother and has spent several years of his life in the UAE, they added. An Israeli official also confirmed his identity. The suspect has been transferred from Saudi Arabia, where the plane landed, to the UAE, where he faces a terrorism investigation. On Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the suspect was believed to have undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination.” An Israeli official told CNN the suspect had worked for Flydubai for only eight months. A third source said the alleged assailant had previously worked for Royal Air Maroc, Morocco’s national carrier. The revelations are likely to raise concerns about the importance of background checks in aviation hiring. CNN has reached out to Oman Air, Royal Air Maroc and the Dubai government’s media office for comment. Flydubai said it could not provide comment while the incident remained under investigation. The new details leave unexplained how a citizen of Oman, which does not recognize Israel, was permitted to serve as a pilot on a flight to Tel Aviv, despite Israel’s stringent aviation security measures. An Israeli official told CNN on Wednesday that several Israeli agencies – including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the Transportation Ministry – were investigating how the Omani pilot came to be part of the flight crew.

articles.title: Film fan goes from home cinema to 470-seat Dumfries movie theatre
articles.summary: Tristan Campbell has been working for two years on his dream to reopen the cinema in Dumfries.
articles.body:
For as long as Tristan Campbell can remember, he has loved the movies.

He has a home cinema in his garage in Elgin but, over the past few years, he has embarked on a project which will see him "scale it up a bit".

In the very near future, he hopes to reopen the 470-seater former Odeon in Dumfries, a venue that closed its doors in 2018, leaving the town without a large-scale cinema.

As side hustles go, they do not come much more ambitious than this.

He is not alone, of course, in his love of film theatres of a certain vintage.

In Prestwick, the community has taken over the Broadway Cinema and is working to bringing it back to its former use.

At a much earlier stage is The Vogue in Glasgow's Possilpark, which was recently saved from demolition but faces an uncertain future.

Stepping back inside the Dumfries venue, it is easy to understand people's fascination with "the pictures".

The main auditorium is so well preserved you would not be surprised to see a choc ice seller tempting you into buying some treats.

Work has been going on for months - much longer than Tristan expected - to bring the facility back into use.

However, the signs went up on the building front this week and he is now hopeful the grand opening is not too far away.

The town battling hard to get its cinema back

Tristan fell in love with the well-preserved Dumfries site straight away but, instead of the matter of weeks he hoped for, it has taken two years to reach a point where reopening is "not far away".

It's a real passion project for a man who grew up in Northern Ireland and now works as a whisky distiller in Speyside.

"It started, I suppose, when I was a kid and going to my local cinema which I enjoyed," he explained.

"It was the Palladium Cinema in Coleraine and then the local multiplex opened up and the cinema that I enjoyed going to went over to bingo, as many of them do.

"The multiplex just wasn't the same for me - there wasn't the same sense of occasion."

So he set out to find a place that could take you back to that era - having already dipped his toes in the water at home.

"I converted my garage into a cinema - I suppose it was like the trial run," he said.

"So if my wife and I fancy watching a film, the neighbours must wonder - what are they up to?

"They'll see us taking a tray each with our dinner out to the garage and closing the door."

Despite the time it has taken, he has enjoyed support from the local community.

"To be honest, that's what's kept me going. It's been two very, very long and very difficult years," he admitted.

"There's been so many hurdles put in our way and so many delays to work getting done for various reasons.

"So it's that goodwill of the people in Dumfries that's kept me going, that's made me think let's persevere with this, it's worthwhile doing."

The staff have been in place for some time and are also ready to go - among their number is the Regal's general manager, Kelly Pritchard from Dumfries.

"I have so many memories of just growing up and being brought to the cinema," she said.

"My mum brought me to come see The Fellowship of the Ring and The Philosopher's Stone right here. I would have been five or six years old and just a massive screen in front of you - it blows your mind when you're that age."

She, too, has a lifelong love of cinema and is excited at the prospect of seeing the place reopen.

"I cannot wait to welcome people through the doors - like I said, it has been a long wait," she said.

Tristan said there had been lots of milestones along the way but the most significant was yet to come.

"The big one, I think, will definitely be opening night when there's bums on seats, there's a film on the screen, and I'll probably just collapse in a heap in the corner," he said.

And why does he think he can succeed where a big operator failed?

"It was actually working for Odeon, it just wasn't part of their core cinema estate," he said.

He said Dumfries "just didn't tick the boxes" for the way the company wanted to go.

"We hope to make it work even better by keeping that community feel about it and getting a real buzz about the place again," he said.

He pointed to Merlin Cinema's takeover of another former Odeon in Ayr as an example of what could be achieved.

"It absolutely can be done - it just needs the focus and the energy behind it," he said.

"It's an experience that you share with other people and you can't beat it."

articles.title: Jared Kushner scolds CNN over 'deeply misleading’ report, says key info buried behind paywall
articles.summary: Jared Kushner fired back at CNN over a report linking his firm Affinity Partners to Israeli defense investments, calling the story misleading.
articles.body: Senior Trump advisor Jared Kushner accused CNN of publishing a "deeply misleading story and headline" suggesting his "diplomatic work in the Middle East somehow benefited investments in Israeli defense companies" in a fiery social media post on Friday. President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, who rarely criticizes the media publicly, took to X to scold a paywall-protected CNN report headlined, "How Jared Kushner’s firm’s investment in an Israeli company could be a major conflict of interest," that was published on Thursday. The report noted that Kushner acted as a key negotiator regarding the war in Gaza while his company, Affinity Partners, "held the largest stake in an Israeli firm backing businesses involved in Israel’s military campaigns." KUSHNER GIVES HAMAS STARK ULTIMATUM: DISARM OR ISRAEL GETS US BACKING TO ‘FINISH THE JOB’ Kushner argued that CNN’s own reporting contradicts the headline, but said readers without a paid subscription to the website were left in the dark. "Buried behind a paywall, it acknowledges: ‘CNN found no indication that Kushner’s actions as a diplomat directly affected the investments reviewed,’" Kushner wrote. Indeed, CNN said it found no indication that Kushner’s actions as a diplomat directly impacted the investments, but that point was buried 10 paragraphs deep and only visible to paid CNN subscribers. The lengthy report said, "CNN used Israeli financial transparency laws to trace some of the military-linked investments of Phoenix Financial, a Tel Aviv-based firm that Kushner’s investment group doubled its stake in last year, shortly before Donald Trump returned to the Oval Office." HILLARY CLINTON BREAKS WITH DEMOCRATIC CRITICS BY BACKING TRUMP’S GAZA PLAN AS THE 'ONLY GAME IN TOWN' "Those records, which include only a fraction of Phoenix’s holdings, show Phoenix has invested hundreds of millions of dollars into Israel’s largest arms manufacturer, Elbit Systems. Phoenix also holds stakes in at least eight other companies providing equipment for the Israeli military ranging from drones to warships to demolition machinery, CNN found," according to the report. "All nine companies identified by CNN saw their stock value climb last year, with many stating the war in Gaza had driven demand for their businesses," the CNN report continued. "Affinity doesn’t directly hold a stake in the nine companies CNN identified — but it does stand to reap rewards when Phoenix makes a profit." CNN also noted that Kushner described Phoenix as a strong investment for Affinity. In his response, Kushner said that Phoenix is not a defense company, despite CNN’s framing, and defended his company’s investments. "It is one of Israel’s largest publicly traded financial institutions, highly regulated and managing approximately $220 billion across thousands of investments," Kushner wrote. "Think of Phoenix as the Israeli equivalent of Vanguard or Fidelity. It manages the retirement savings of millions of Israelis. The savers don’t choose the individual investments, and neither do I," Kushner continued. "I have no role in deciding what Phoenix buys or sells. It has performed very well for Affinity and our investors, up more than five times since our initial investment." Kushner added that Affinity is an SEC-registered investment firm. "Our investment in Phoenix is public and dates to before President Trump was re-elected, and before I returned to public service. Affinity does not own the defense companies highlighted in CNN’s story," Kushner wrote. "Those facts make for a less provocative headline, but a much more accurate story," he continued. "Misleading stories will not distract me from the work President Trump asked me to do: help end wars, bring people together and pursue peace. That work is too important." A CNN spokesperson told Fox News Digital that "we stand by our reporting." KUSHNER TOUTS UNPRECEDENTED IRAN CONTACTS AS TEHRAN DENIES TRUMP BACKCHANNEL In a separate post, Kushner said he has ignored "false and misleading stories" for the past decade, but "the cycle has gotten out of control where old lies get repeated as fact, new ones get added, and the record becomes increasingly distorted," so he felt a need to respond. CNN published a statement from Kushner's attorney, which was also hidden behind the paywall. "Any suggestion that Jared’s diplomatic work influenced Phoenix’s investments in the companies you identify, or vice versa, is incorrect," the attorney told CNN. articles.title: Flydubai pilot recounts cockpit stabbing in call with Indian PM Modi
articles.summary: Smit Machchhar recalls midair disaster after co-pilot’s attack on Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv.
articles.body:
Indian pilot Smit Machchhar, who was stabbed by his co-pilot in an alleged attempt to crash a Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv, has shared a public account of how he managed to open the cockpit door and let passengers take control of the plane despite his injuries.

Speaking on Friday from a hospital bed in Abu Dhabi via video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Machchhar said that he knew the aircraft was going down as he lay bleeding on the floor.

“I had suffered so many injuries that I had collapsed. At that time, I could feel that the aircraft was going down . I knew this was the last push, that the door was right there,” he said in a nearly 10-minute video released on the prime minister’s social media channels.

He added: “I was being hit even then, but I just opened the door and everyone came in.”

Machchhar, who has 17 years of aviation experience, including 11 as a captain, said that experience helped him grasp what was happening even while wounded.

He told Modi he had recited a Hindu devotional prayer during the ordeal.

“I know God himself saved me,” he said, in an emotional exchange with Modi, who is from the same home state of Gujarat.

Modi praised Machchhar’s bravery, saying his presence of mind had saved lives and the reputation of Indian pilots.

Machchhar said he allowed passengers and crew to overpower the co-pilot and let a second pair of Flydubai pilots take control and land the plane in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

The Flydubai flight was carrying 174 people as it briefly plunged around 17,000 feet (5,180 metres) before it was brought back under control.

UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash has called the incident a “terrorist act”, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the co-pilot had undergone “Islamist radical indoctrination” and appeared “suicidal”.

US President Donald Trump has warned that Iran would be “hit very hard” if found to be linked to the attack.

The United Arab Emirates has said it will launch an investigation into the incident.

articles.title: Congress abruptly replaces Ajay Rai as state chief in poll-bound UP
articles.summary: LUCKNOW/CHANDIGARH: Congress overhauled its PCC brass in two poll-bound states Friday, installing Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana \"Mona\" Mishra as the UP unit
articles.body: LUCKNOW/CHANDIGARH: Congress overhauled its PCC brass in two poll-bound states Friday, installing Rampur Khas MLA Aradhana "Mona" Mishra as the UP unit chief and hockey Olympian Pargat Singh as state president in Punjab, with each pick engineered around caste arithmetic ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.In UP, Ajay Rai was abruptly replaced by Mishra while Saharanpur MP Imran Masood was named working president. The pairing brings together a Brahmin face from eastern UP and a Muslim with influence in the west, striking a caste-regional balance the party rounded out by appointing Rajendra Pal Gautam, a Dalit, as state in-charge.Mishra (52), CLP chief in the UP assembly since 2019 and daughter of Rajya Sabha member Pramod Tiwari, is considered close to the central brass. She entered the assembly through a 2014 bypoll and retained Rampur Khas in 2017 and 2022, having earlier served as block pramukh of Sangramgarh from 2002 to 2014.Mishra's rapport with SP as seat-sharing talks gather pace is seen as a significant factor in the party making its choice. "Unlike Ajay Rai, Mishra has maintained an amicable equation with the SP brass. Her being the face of the state Congress could make coordination between the two parties smoother," a source said, though the two INDIA bloc partners are yet to settle their 2027 arrangement.In Punjab, the choice of Pargat Singh, who captained India at the 1992 and 1996 Olympics, came within hours of Amarinder Singh Raja Warring handing his resignation as state chief to Rahul Gandhi. Warring congratulated Pargat, as did former CM Charanjit Singh Channi, whose supporters had revolted against the outgoing chief.Struggling to contain factionalism, the party settled on a Jat Sikh face acceptable to both camps. Pargat (61) was seen with the Channi camp during the July-Aug crisis but pushed for consensus and direct talks with the party brass. articles.title: US road rage killer's sentence quashed because AI video of victim was shown in court
articles.summary: The Arizona appeals court ruled that airing an AI message from the dead victim "crossed that line".
articles.body:
An Arizona road rage killer will be resentenced after an appeals court ruled that an AI-generated video message from his dead victim was improperly aired in court.

Gabriel Paul Horcasitas was found guilty by a jury of shooting and killing Christopher Pelkey, 37, during a confrontation at a red light in 2021. He was sentenced to 10 years behind bars.

But his legal team appealed, arguing that the trial judge should not have allowed an AI video, created by Pelkey's family, to be shown in court ahead of last year's sentencing.

The Arizona Court of Appeals agreed, ruling that Horcasitas, 55, must be resentenced because the AI clip "crossed that line".

"Rather than document an event or recording a particular moment, the AI video presents a depiction of the victim and his thoughts created from the imaginings of the victim's sister," the court of appeals wrote on Wednesday.

Horcasitas' lawyer, Kristen Reller, who filed the appeal, declined to comment.

Jessica Gattuso, an attorney for victims in the case, did not respond to a request for comment.

Pelkey's sister, Stacey Wales, told the BBC last year the family had used voice recordings, videos and pictures to recreate him for the AI video.

"To Gabriel Horcasitas, the man who shot me, it is a shame we encountered each other that day in those circumstances," said the AI version of Pelkey in court in 2025. "In another life, we probably could have been friends."

"I believe in forgiveness, and a God who forgives. I always have and I still do," the AI version of Pelkey - wearing a grey baseball cap - continued.

At the time of the sentencing, the judge who oversaw the case, Todd Lang, seemed to appreciate the use of AI.

"I loved that AI, thank you for that. As angry as you are, as justifiably angry as the family is, I heard the forgiveness," Judge Lang said. "I feel that that was genuine."

articles.title: Women given free shorts at Oktoberfest to prevent upskirting
articles.summary: The step at the Munich festival comes after thousands of voyeuristic videos emerged on social media.
articles.body:
The operator of a popular amusement ride at the Munich Oktoberfest has been handing out free cycling shorts to women, after thousands of voyeuristic videos emerged on social media.

Some videos showing women on the Teufelsrad , or Devil's Wheel, have been viewed millions of times. One is said to have made thousands of euros for a woman who posted it online.

The Teufelsrad is one of the oldest attractions at the Oktoberfest, the annual beer festival which comes to an end this weekend after 16 days. Its circular platform rotates faster and faster until its riders fall off, and the motion and speed often make skirts fly up.

Filming under skirts is illegal in Germany, and carries a two-year sentence in jail.

However, critics believe the law does not go far enough, and the videos of women on the Teufelsrad in their traditional dirndl dresses often show their underwear. Sometimes, the images have been digitally altered to show them naked, according to local broadcaster BR.

One woman made €9,000 (£7,650) from a single clip, according to BR, whose investigations found that a group of professional YouTubers from Ukraine and several people from Bavaria were behind the videos.

At least 32,000 videos of women on the Teufelsrad have been in circulation, according to Munich-based daily Süddeutsche Zeitung. Some have apparently been viewed millions of times.

The operator of the Teufelsrad, Elisabeth Polaczy, told the BBC that, for the past three years, she has been handing out free cycling shorts to women and girls wearing dresses, to protect them from people filming in the crowd.

This Oktoberfest she has handed out more than 100 pairs, she says: "I want to do everything I can to make people feel secure."

Polaczy, who is now 80, said donating cycling shorts wasn't cheap, but it was worth it for her own peace of mind.

The Teufelsrad tent is hung with signs and police posters in German and English warning against filming under people's skirts, but Polaczy says it is impossible to control everyone filming with smart phones.

Some waitresses at this year's beer festival say they have also started wearing cycling shorts under their dirndls.

A spokesman for the Bavarian police told the BBC that since 2025, it has run a poster campaign at the Oktoberfest, warning against upskirting.

This year, police arrested a 45-year-old Swiss man for using his phone to film under a German woman's dirndl. Last year there were 10 arrests for upskirting and seven in 2024.

However, Josephine Ballon, who heads German non-profit organisation Hate Aid, which aims to support victims of digital violence, told the BBC that the current law against upskirting does not provide enough protection.

Although she says there are plans for a new law, current legislation "applies only when you film under the skirt", and not when a skirt simply flies up and gets photographed.

The new camera glasses are also a threat, she believes.

Ballon wants anyone who has uploaded intimate pictures of women on the internet to be punished, along with the platforms that put them up.

Meanwhile, the city of Munich has sought to tighten up on influencers and content creators who earn money from their social media postings and who want to film at the Oktoberfest.

Munich has banned broadcasting live streams from the festival and requires anyone who wants to film there to hold a permit, which is issued by the city for a fee.

Hundreds of licences have been issued this year to influencers, who make money from product placement or sponsoring.

A comedian, a journalist, an actor and a TV presenter walk into a church. But sadly, the punchline for one of them was becoming the first victim of this year's Celebrity Traitors.

As Friday's episode got under way, a delicious new twist saw traitors Richard E Grant and Maya Jama invite James Acaster to join them in the turret, and simultaneously murder a fellow player.

Unfortunately, it fell to Amol Rajan to become the Paloma Faith of this series - being taken away in a coffin in episode two before even having the chance to take part in a banishment.

"It's gutting to be the first out," Rajan said afterwards, noting that perhaps it was because he had been "a bit bullish with Richard" earlier in the day.

"But you know what, games are games, and just as there are winners, so there have to be losers."

The next morning, presenter Claudia Winkleman confirmed the University Challenge host's murder to the other players, joking: "That's what I call a starter for 10."

Acaster, meanwhile, reflected: "I'm gutted to not be a faithful anymore, I don't like lying. But if I don't join them, they'll kill me." You can't fault his logic.

The decision meant that Grant, an Oscar-nominated actor with a Razzie-worthy traitor strategy, did at least manage to commit one successful murder despite his shambolic first day.

The 69-year-old spent much of Friday's episode trying to repair the damage from his earlier exchange in the bar, where he blurted out that he was a traitor to Joe Lycett, Rob Beckett and several others.

Obviously a man who made such an excellent Spice Girls manager in the 1997 masterpiece Spice World: The Movie is hard for anyone to picture as a traitor, so many other players assumed Grant was attempting some elaborate double bluff.

Jama is off to a much stronger start. "I am quite shocked at my ability to just lie to everyone," the Love Island host said in the castle's diary room. "I'm an all-or-nothing kind of honey."

As the players gathered for breakfast, other theories began to surface. Mathematician Hannah Fry said she had spotted Leigh-Anne Pinnock putting on make-up late in the evening, perhaps heading to the turret.

"I think it's James," declared Jerry Hall, suddenly giving viewers hope that the new cast will be better traitor hunters than last year's. Until she clarified that she was talking about James Blunt, not Acaster.

As the players prepared to head out for the mission, conversations turned to far more important matters. "Do you have more teeth than a normal person?" Grant asked Rob Beckett.

The players headed out to the mission, which had the usual slightly convoluted rules that took Winkleman quite a while to explain.

In a nutshell, the celebrities were to be buried alive in pairs, with only one duo left above ground.

Ross Kemp was pre-selected by the traitors to be protected from burial along with his grave partner Romesh Ranganathan, who did a delightful dance when he found out he wouldn't be going underground.

Kemp and Ranganathan then had the opportunity to dig up some gold graves which would add to the prize pot, or alternatively dig up and free their fellow players.

They opted for the latter, with some of the other players struggling to get the soil off their faces. In the end, all the celebrities were released, with the exception of Fry and Hall.

The pair were freed early after Hall shouted "Haggis!" – effectively a Scottish version of "I'm a celebrity get me out of here!" - because she was visibly uncomfortable being buried alive.

It might have led to an early release, but it ultimately guaranteed that either she or Fry will be murdered next, unless the traitors recruit again.

"Just you and me up for murder," Fry told her afterwards. "You'd better not be a traitor or I'm really screwed!"

In a flashback shown to viewers, Acaster explained the decision to protect Kemp from burial, telling his fellow traitors: "I think if we give it to Ross, he'll overthink it, and behave in a way that would draw suspicion."

Very clever. "You're a wonderful traitor," observed Grant. (Certainly better than him.)

Finally, it was time for the first banishment of the series, with Grant still in damage control mode.

"I have a slight pinprick of advantage," he told himself in the castle's diary room. "Nobody would possibly believe that anybody would be so stupid as to come forward and say 'I am a traitor'. I'm hoping that I do get away with it."

His fellow traitors clearly wanted to be supportive, but things were getting dicey.

Acaster described him as a "loose cannon", while Jama said: "I want to save him, even though he's dug himself the biggest hole imaginable."

Back in the castle, Ranganathan pointed out: "If somebody else had behaved like Richard, we wouldn't even be having a debate about this, you would just go 'you've got to vote for him'."

But others had a slightly different take. "Richard feels a little too easy," reflected actress Myha'la, "and then anybody pushing him feels suspicious to me."

Comedian Joanne McNally agreed some players were "using him as a fall guy and a decoy," although she did admit later that he's "made such a shambles of it now".

As discussions got going, it took a surprisingly long time for Grant's name to come up, as the other players debate other suspects such as Julie Hesmondhalgh.

The actress aroused suspicion because she was the first celebrity this year to receive a shield. The group seem to have overlooked she only got that - in the opening minutes of the first show - after the other contestants voted her the most trustworthy.

But as discussion turned to Grant, Hesmondhalgh put forward one of the most convincing cases of the night.

"You came into the bar, and said you were a traitor," she told him. "It was a bold move. It was chaotic and we love you for your chaos.

"I think we are at risk of being the most idiotic group of faithfuls in the world, if we go for someone else tonight based on nothing at all, when somebody has come into the room and said 'I am a traitor'. There's no reason to say it unless you are."

Miranda Hart agreed that "the joy when he took off his blindfold" when Winkleman first selected the traitors made Grant look suspicious.

Viewers will have to wait until the next episode to see how the round table goes, as the episode finished before voting had even started.

(It's worth saying that, as cliffhangers go, this was far less irritating than ending an episode in the middle of a roundtable, as producers often do.)

"You've given us all a problem," Ranganathan told Grant as the episode drew to a close and the players prepared to vote. "By doing that, it was a big mistake by you, I feel like you forced our hand."

Admittedly, it's not looking good - the round table is shaping up to be a landslide vote against Grant. But we still wouldn't bet against him.

"I do not go down without a fight," he concluded. "I did not survive four decades in showbusiness without a fight."

Celebrity Traitors continues on Thursday at 20:00 BST on BBC One and iPlayer.

articles.body: Twitch streamer Lindsay “Lyndi” has shared a personal account of what she says was a difficult and abusive relationship after the recent Cornell University sexual assault case drew attention online. In a nine-page Google document titled “My side”, Lyndi said she had survived domestic and sexual assault/abuse and wanted to speak about her own experience. She also addressed past claims involving her former partner, streamer Neil “RatedEpicz”, including allegations that she blackmailed him. Lyndi said she accepts responsibility for things she did wrong but believes that does not erase what she says she went through.Lindsay “Lyndi” explains her relationship with Neil “RatedEpicz”Lyndi said her relationship with Neil “RatedEpicz” started well but later became difficult. She claimed he accused her of dating him for “clout” and called her several names. She said the arguments became worse and affected how she viewed herself.“We started dating, and like any other relationship, we instantly clicked. We were good for a few months until he started to accuse me of dating him for ‘clout’ and began to call me a leech, among other names. This happened multiple times throughout our relationship. The fighting had gotten worse and worse, the names more vile like ‘e st, wre’. This screenshot is included bc idgaf, he made me so insecure about my own ‘friend.’”She also described the relationship as controlling. According to her account, she was not allowed to speak to men, play with some friends, use VRChat or freely take part in roleplay. She later said she found out that her former partner had been unfaithful during the relationship.“Meanwhile, I had later found out he was cheating on me since the start of our relationship, and I don’t even know how many women total it was. I had only found this out at the end of our relationship. You can call me stupid for not assuming so because he didn’t allow me to tell a single soul we had dated. I felt isolated, scared to say anything…”Lyndi denies blackmail claim and takes responsibility for her actionsLyndi also responded to claims that she had blackmailed RatedEpicz. She said messages about money came while she was dealing with his alleged infidelity and worrying about their apartment and finances. She denied sharing his private information and made a separate allegation about a threat involving intimate images.“I never blackmailed him. I never shared his public information. If that is blackmail, then the time he had threatened to leak my nudes on Reddit was also blackmail. This relationship was incredibly toxic, start to finish.”Lyndi said she does not consider herself blameless. She acknowledged that some of the words and actions she used were wrong and said she has apologised to people she hurt.“The words I used were and still are unacceptable; I will take responsibility every single time, and I have apologized and will continue to apologize to the people I’ve hurt. Our relationship was terrible, but I didn’t deserve the things that I endured. Thank you for reading; use your voice. You are not small. Don’t be silenced.”The statement came after the Cornell case involving a former student known as Jane Doe gained renewed attention. The student filed a civil lawsuit alleging that she was drugged and sexually assaulted by multiple Chi Phi fraternity members in 2024. articles.title: Could El Niño mean there are no Atlantic hurricanes this year?
articles.summary: For the first time in three decades there has not been a single Atlantic hurricane in September, normally the most active month.
articles.body:
For the first time in more than 30 years, a hurricane has not formed in the Atlantic throughout September - normally the most active month for hurricane activity.

The eerily quiet season continues and with just two months left, there is an increasing possibility that no hurricanes will develop at all.

This would make the 2026 Atlantic hurricane season the only one in the satellite era without a hurricane.

The biggest reason for this is El Niño, which traditionally stifles activity in the Atlantic but brings a very active season in the eastern North Pacific.

The Atlantic hurricane season was predicted to be quieter than normal as a result of this.

With a very strong El Niño forecast, the US National Hurricane Center in May predicted a total of eight to 14 named storms. Of those, three to six were predicted to become hurricanes, with one to three becoming major hurricanes.

September is typically the most active month for tropical storm and hurricane activity.

But, this year marks the latest date on record since the start of the satellite era (1960s onward) where no hurricane has formed in the North Atlantic.

There were, however, four named tropical storms which formed in September: Edouard, Fay, Gonzalo and Hanna.

All but Edouard stayed out in the open waters of the Atlantic.

The National Hurricane Center suggests there is no sign of any tropical storm activity or hurricane over the next week at least.

Forecasters at Colorado State University, who also monitor activity, suggest the strong El Niño is likely to disrupt wind patterns across the Atlantic and "likely result in below-normal activity" over the next two-weeks.

As the typical peak of the season has passed and is now on a downward trend until 30 November, a season without a single hurricane is looking increasingly possible.

In the historical Atlantic hurricane database, there has not been a year without a hurricane recorded since 1914. However, this was pre-satellite monitoring so it is impossible to say with certainty that none formed.

How does El Niño affect tropical development?

While El Niño is the natural warming of the tropical Pacific, it can disrupt weather patterns around the globe.

As wind patterns shift during an El Niño, upper winds over the Atlantic increase and this leads to more wind shear, where wind changes rapidly with height.

Increased wind shear rips apart thunderstorms, preventing them from growing into tropical storms or hurricanes.

Meanwhile, the Pacific typically becomes more active during El Niño because the sea surface temperatures here are much higher, combined with more favourable wind patterns.

The warmer waters give storms more energy to grow into tropical storms and hurricanes.

This year, temperature records have already been broken in a key region of the central-eastern Pacific, with daily sea surface temperatures now exceeding the previous record set during the very strong El Niño of 2015.

There have so far been 17 named storms in the basin including nine hurricanes, seven of which were major.

In terms of the amount of energy these storms have produced - known as the Accumulated Cyclone Energy - this season is around two and half times more active than normal at this point.

El Niño is predicted to continue to strengthen with forecasts suggesting it will reach its peak in November or December.
